COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
WPSS/542/2026
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Amar Murti Shukla, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Dinesh Bankoti, Brief Holder for the
State.
Mr. T.A. Khan, Senior Advocate for the
Sugar Factory.
2. Petitioner applied for compassionate
appointment after death of his father, who
passed away on 12.11.2018. His application was
rejected vide order dated 20.05.2025 only on the
ground of delay. It is mentioned in the order that
application should have been made within three
years.
3. It is contended by learned counsel for
petitioner that as per Dying in Harness Rules,
1974, applicable in respect of State employees,
application for compassionate appointment can
be made within five years from the date of
death. It is thus contended that period of three
years referred to in the impugned order, is
extremely short and it has no statutory basis.
4. Mr. T.A. Khan, learned Senior Counsel
appearing for Sugar Mill relies upon the policy
decision taken by Uttarakhand Cooperative
Sugar Mill Federation Limited on 15.11.2011.
In para 14 of the said policy decision, it is
mentioned that application for compassionate

2026:UHC:2828
appointment can be made by the dependent of a
deceased employee within three years from the
date of death.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner,
however, submits that although the policy
provides for the period within which application
has to be made, however, consequence of not
making application within three years is not
indicated in the policy. Thus it is contended that
provision contained in para 14 is to be treated as
directory and not mandatory.
6. This Court finds substance in the
submission made by learned counsel for the
petitioner.
7. Although the outer limit for making
application is indicated in para 14 of the policy
framed by Uttarakhand Cooperative Sugar Mills
Federation Limited; however, consequence of
not making application within three years is not
indicated, thus para 14 has to be treated as
directory and not mandatory.
8. Even otherwise also, State Government is
having all pervasive administrative control over
Bazpur Cooperative Sugar Factory Limited, its
General Manager is an officer of the State
Government belonging to Provincial Civil
Service; and substantial amount of funds are
provided by the State Government each year for
running the sugar mill, therefore, there cannot

2026:UHC:2828
be any doubt that the sugar mill falls within the
meaning of State, as defined under Article 12 of
the Constitution.
9. The provision for compassionate
appointment is made by the Apex body of the
State run Sugar Mills in keeping with its role as
model employer to provide succour to the
unfortunate family members, who are rendered
penniless due to death of sole bread earner.
Therefore, rejection of petitioner's application
for compassionate appointment merely because
there was delay of about 11⁄2 months, does not
appear to be proper.
10. The impugned rejection order is, therefore,
liable to be quashed and is hereby quashed.
11. The writ petition is allowed. The
competent authority is directed to reconsider
petitioner's claim for compassionate
appointment, on merit, within six weeks from
date of presentation of certified copy of this
order.
(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 18.04.2026 Mahinder/
